events.title: US credit downgrade
events.blurb: S&P cut the US government's AAA credit rating on August 5, 2011, in the middle of the euro-area debt crisis.

events.title: China devaluation
events.blurb: China devalued the yuan on August 11, 2015; global stocks slid and US markets had a chaotic open on August 24.

events.title: Volmageddon
events.blurb: On February 5, 2018 the VIX more than doubled in a single day, wiping out funds that had bet on calm markets.

events.title: Christmas Eve selloff
events.blurb: Rising interest rates and trade-war worries drove a slide through the end of 2018 that bottomed on Christmas Eve.

events.title: COVID-19 crash
events.blurb: As the pandemic spread in February and March 2020, the S&P 500 had its fastest fall into a bear market on record.

events.title: Rate shock
events.blurb: The Federal Reserve raised rates at the fastest pace in decades to fight inflation, and stocks fell through most of the year.

events.title: Yen carry-trade unwind
events.blurb: A Bank of Japan rate hike and weak US jobs data triggered a global selloff that peaked on August 5, 2024.

events.title: Tariff shock
events.blurb: Sweeping US tariffs announced on April 2, 2025 set off one of the sharpest two-day drops in the S&P 500's history.
